extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors reporting cross-sectional observational studies (epidemiologists, public-health researchers, clinical investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist for transparent reporting of cross-sectional observational studies in manuscripts—what items to include in title/abstract, intro, methods, results, discussion, and other information. Designed to guide authors preparing reports and reviewers/editors assessing completeness of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Indicate the study’s design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract. (b) Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the design explicit in title/abstract (e.g., 'cross-sectional study') and ensure the abstract summarizes methods and key results in a balanced, informative way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background/rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context motivating the study question and why the cross-sectional approach is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state primary and, if appropriate, secondary objectives and any hypotheses tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design (methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe that the study is cross-sectional, timing of measurements, and key design features up front (e.g., sampling frame, one-time measurement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geographic, institutional, and temporal details so readers can judge context and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants (methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe inclusion/exclusion criteria, sampling strategy, recruitment procedures, and any selection filters that affect representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide operational definitions and diagnostic or cutoff criteria so variables are reproducible and interpretable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources/measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement). Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State instruments, assays, questionnaires, measurement protocols, and any validation/reliability information. If groups were assessed differently, describe comparability and harmonization. (Where relevant: give information separately for exposed and unexposed groups.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report steps taken to minimize selection bias, information bias, confounding, and other systematic errors (e.g., blinding of assessors, standardized data collection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study size
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size calculations, assumptions, precision considerations, or practical constraints that determined size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses. If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State any transformations, categorizations (with boundaries), and rationale for grouping continuous measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (b) Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions. (c) Explain how missing data were addressed. (d) If applicable, describe analytical methods taking account of sampling strategy. (e) Describe any sensitivity analyses. Provide enough detail for replication and for judging appropriateness of analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants (results)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study—e.g., numbers potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included in the study, completing follow-up, and analysed. (b) Give reasons for non-participation at each stage. (c) Consider use of a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and attrition information, with reasons for exclusions or non-participation; include a flow diagram where helpful to show participant flow through stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive data
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give characteristics of study participants (eg demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders. (b) Indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present baseline/descriptive tables reporting distributions of covariates and exposures, and report missingness per variable. (Where relevant: give information separately for exposed and unexposed groups.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts or summary statistics for primary and secondary outcomes so results are transparent and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main results
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (eg, 95% confidence interval). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included. (b) Report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorized. (c) If relevant, consider translating estimates of relative risk into absolute risk for a meaningful time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report effect estimates with measures of precision and clearly state adjustment sets and rationale; provide category cutpoints and, where helpful, present absolute risks to aid interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done—eg analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present results of planned and exploratory subgroup, interaction, and sensitivity analyses, and indicate which were prespecified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results (discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key results with reference to study objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin discussion with concise summary of main findings aligned to stated objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about threats to validity, likely direction of bias (over- or under-estimation), and the potential impact on conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place findings in context of prior evidence, avoid overstatement, and discuss consistency, plausibility, and alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider population, setting, and study procedures to judge how widely findings can be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and any funder involvement in design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of STROBE Explanation and Elaboration article
rubrics_metrics.description: The STROBE checklist is best used in conjunction with the Explanation and Elaboration article which discusses each checklist item and gives methodological background and published examples of transparent reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Explanation & Elaboration article and STROBE website for expanded guidance, methodological background, and examples; links provided to PLoS Medicine, Annals of Internal Medicine, Epidemiology, and strobe-statement.org.
